newsitem.title: USA: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies seen lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies seen lower.

text.p: Early calls on CME hog futures ranged from up 0.100 cent per lb to off 0.200 while pork bellies were called 0.100 to 0.300 cent a lb lower, livestock analysts said.

Steadier-than-expected cash hog indications early Wednesday could lend support to nearby hog futures after losses were pared late Tuesday. Bull spreading and unwinding of bear spreads is also likely on the modest hog marketings, analysts said.
However, a continued slide in cash pork prices, negative packer margins and a lower CME lean hog index will likely keep pressure on the market, sources said.
The latest CME lean hog index was off $0.33 at $76.02 per cwt.

Although the out-of-town report was called neutral overall, an increase in deliverable stocks could pressure pork belly futures early. Steady to lower cash belly prices, despite reduced slaughter, were also expected to weigh on futures, analysts said.

CME reported a net in-movement of 24,000 lbs last week in the out-of-town report which compared with early trade estimates of unchanged to in 500,000 lbs. But deliverable stocks rose to 7.2 million from 6.28 million lbs.
